audit: JPL Horizons one-hour versus six-hour sample sensitivity
source: JPL Horizons Sun 10 / Earth 399, observer coord@301, 2026-11-14 through 2026-11-18, APPARENT=AIRLESS, QUANTITIES=4
method: Sampled left-endpoint visibility against the same existing 6-km NASA LOLA-derived skyline with 2-m observer; 1h and 6h calculations use identical geometry thresholds. Energy figures not considered in the primary comparison.
limitations: One-hour ephemeris calculations were checked in an Internet-connected scientific environment, but the complete hourly data are not embedded in this release.
The local skyline covers 6 km only; remote terrain and a real communications budget are not modeled.
One-hour sampling does not yield exact rise and set times. An adaptive event finder is still required.
The SPICE/Horizons comparison validates ephemeris implementations, not terrain classification or flight safety.
conclusion: The previously published 18h number should not be presented without its 6h sampling qualifier; at 1h the same local geometric model yields 21h. Use the finer sample for illustrative narrative and maintain 6h figures only with explicit cadence labels.
